predecessors.name: Golden Horde
predecessors.text: the Crimean peninsula and the steppe 'between the Dnieper and the Donets'

successors.name: Russian Empire
successors.text: the whole peninsula, annexed as the Taurida Oblast

ledger.x: March 1441: Hacı I Giray is named khan of Crimea.
1449: Hacı I Giray takes the throne and moves the capital to Qırq Yer.
1532: Bahçeseray, 'founded in 1532 by Sahib I Giray', becomes the khans' seat.
1572: the Azov and Kuban strip stays with the Nogais.
1738: the Kuban strip passes to the khanate as Cliopatria's Small Horde row ends.
July 1771: the Russian army occupies Crimea.
November 1772: the Russian occupation gives way to the treaty.
November 1772: the khanate takes the former Kaffa Eyalet.
21 July 1774: Kerch and Yenikale go to Russia.
8 April 1783 (O.S.): Russia annexes the Crimean Khanate.

wars.name: Great Horde raids on Crimea under Sayid Ahmad (1445, 1452)
wars.outcome: 'In 1445, Sayid unsuccessfully besieged Perekop'; Sayid's 1452 raid 'ended with Sayid's defeat by Hacı'.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of the Crimean coast (1475)
wars.outcome: Ottoman forces under Gedik Ahmet Pasha conquered Theodoro and the Genoese colonies in 1475 (Mangup surrendered at the end of December 1475); Meñli I Giray was imprisoned three years for resisting and then accepted Ottoman suzerainty.

wars.name: Crimean war on the Great Horde (1502)
wars.outcome: Meñli I Giray 'defeated the last khan of the Great Horde', ending its claims on Crimea; the page names no land that passed to the khanate.

wars.name: Crimean invasion of Russia and Battle of Molodi (1571-1572)
wars.outcome: Devlet I Giray sacked and burned Moscow in 1571; in 1572 the horde crossed the Oka on 26 July and was destroyed in the fighting of 29 July to 2 August.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1735-1739), Crimean campaigns
wars.outcome: Russian armies stormed Perekop (May 1736), took Bakhchisarai on 17 June 1736 and burned Karasubazar on 14 July 1737, losing half their strength; the Treaty of Niš had Russia abandon its claims to Crimea, and Azak was demolished and its lands made neutral.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774) in Crimea
wars.outcome: Russia marched into Kaffa in July 1771; the Treaty of Karasu Bazaar (November 1772) proclaimed an independent khanate; the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca (21 July 1774) made the Tatars 'politically independent' and left Kerch, Yenikale, Kinburn and Azov to Russia.

wars.name: Russian annexation of Crimea (1776-1783)
wars.outcome: Russia invaded in November 1776, took Perekop and installed Şahin Giray (January 1777); Russian forces crushed a revolt at Yeni-Kale in February 1778; the Ottomans signed the Convention of Aynali Kavak in early 1779; a rebellion from 1781 ended with the khan…

certainty.note: The steppe frontier with the Don Cossacks, the Zaporozhian host and the Nogai hordes is approximate throughout.

sources.title: Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Empire
